sanskrit: sa dharmam āhūya purā maharṣir idam uktavān iṣīkayā mayā bālyād ekā viddhā śakuntikā
english: That great seer, summoning Dharma of old, said this: 'In my childhood I pierced a little bird with a reed-stalk.'

sanskrit: tat kilbiṣaṃ smare dharma nānyat pāpam ahaṃ smare tan me sahasrasamitaṃ kasmān nehājayat tapaḥ
english: That sin I remember, O Dharma — no other evil do I remember. Why then has not my austerity, which is equal to a thousand, conquered it here?

sanskrit: garīyān brāhmaṇavadhaḥ sarvabhūtavadhād yataḥ tasmāt tvaṃ kilbiṣād asmāc chūdrayonau janiṣyasi
english: Since the slaying of a brahmin is graver than the slaying of all other beings, therefore, on account of this sin, you shall be born in a shudra womb.

sanskrit: tena śāpena dharmo 'pi śūdrayonāv ajāyata vidvān vidurarūpeṇa dhārmī tanur akilbiṣī
english: By that curse, Dharma himself was born in a shudra womb — learned, in the form of Vidura, a righteous body free from sin.

sanskrit: saṃjayo munikalpas tu jajñe sūto gavalgaṇāt sūryāc ca kuntikanyāyāṃ jajñe karṇo mahārathaḥ sahajaṃ kavacaṃ bibhrat kuṇḍaloddyotitānanaḥ
english: Sañjaya, resembling a sage, was born as a charioteer's son from Gavalgaṇa. And from the Sun, in the maiden daughter of Kuntī, was born Karṇa the great warrior, bearing congenital armor, his face radiant with earrings.

sanskrit: anugrahārthaṃ lokānāṃ viṣṇur lokanamaskṛtaḥ vasudevāt tu devakyāṃ prādurbhūto mahāyaśāḥ
english: For the benefit of the worlds, Viṣṇu, revered by the world, the greatly glorious one, manifested himself from Vāsudeva through Devakī.

sanskrit: anādinidhano devaḥ sa kartā jagataḥ prabhuḥ avyaktam akṣaraṃ brahma pradhānaṃ nirguṇātmakam
english: That god, without beginning or end, is the maker and lord of the universe — the unmanifest, imperishable Brahman, the primal cause, of the nature of that which is beyond qualities.

sanskrit: ātmānam avyayaṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ prabhavaṃ param puruṣaṃ viśvakarmāṇaṃ sattvayogaṃ dhruvākṣaram
english: He is the imperishable Self, the supreme source of Nature, the Cosmic Person, the maker of the universe, the union with pure being, the eternal and imperishable.

sanskrit: anantam acalaṃ devaṃ haṃsaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum dhātāram ajaraṃ nityaṃ tam āhuḥ param avyayam
english: Infinite, immovable, divine, the Swan, Nārāyaṇa the lord, the Sustainer, unaging, eternal — they call him the supreme and imperishable.

sanskrit: puruṣaḥ sa vibhuḥ kartā sarvabhūtapitāmahaḥ dharmasaṃvardhanārthāya prajajñe 'ndhakavṛṣṇiṣu
english: That all-pervading Person, the maker, the grandfather of all beings, was born among the Andhaka-Vṛṣṇis for the purpose of upholding righteousness.

sanskrit: astrajñau tu mahāvīryau sarvaśastraviśāradau sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmā ca nārāyaṇam anuvratau satyakād dhṛdikāc caiva jajñāte 'straviśāradau
english: Sātyaki and Kṛtavarmā, both of great valor, skilled in all weapons and expert in missiles, devoted followers of Nārāyaṇa, were born from Satyaka and Hridika respectively, both masters of arms.

sanskrit: bharadvājasya ca skannaṃ droṇyāṃ śukram avardhata maharṣer ugratapasas tasmād droṇo vyajāyata
english: The seed spilled from Bharadvaja developed in a vessel; from that severe-ascetic great seer's seed, Droṇa was born.

sanskrit: gautamān mithunaṃ jajñe śarastambāc charadvataḥ aśvatthāmnaś ca jananī kṛpaś caiva mahābalaḥ aśvatthāmā tato jajñe droṇād astrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: From Sharadvan of the Gautama line, a pair was born from a clump of reeds — the mother of Aśvatthāmā and Kṛpa the mighty. Aśvatthāmā was then born from Droṇa, the foremost among bearers of weapons.

sanskrit: tathaiva dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi sākṣād agnisamadyutiḥ vaitāne karmaṇi tate pāvakāt samajāyata vīro droṇavināśāya dhanuṣā saha vīryavān
english: Likewise Dhṛṣṭadyumna too, directly blazing like fire, was born from the sacred fire when a Vedic rite was being performed — the valiant hero, born with a bow, destined to destroy Droṇa.

sanskrit: tathaiva vedyāṃ kṛṣṇāpi jajñe tejasvinī śubhā vibhrājamānā vapuṣā bibhratī rūpam uttamam
english: Likewise from the sacrificial altar was born Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) as well — radiant, auspicious, resplendent of form, bearing a most exquisite beauty.

sanskrit: prahrādaśiṣyo nagnajit subalaś cābhavat tataḥ tasya prajā dharmahantrī jajñe devaprakopanāt
english: Nagnajit, a pupil of Prahlāda, became Subala; his offspring, destroyers of dharma, were born due to the wrath of the gods.

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaputro 'bhūc chakuniḥ saubalas tathā duryodhanasya mātā ca jajñāte 'rthavidāv ubhau
english: The son of the king of Gāndhāra became Śakuni, the son of Subala; and the mother of Duryodhana — both were born, those two knowers of worldly affairs.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāj jajñe dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ kṣetre vicitravīryasya pāṇḍuś caiva mahābalaḥ
english: From Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa) were born Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, and the mighty Pāṇḍu as well, in the field of Vichitraveerya.

sanskrit: pāṇḍos tu jajñire pañca putrā devasamāḥ pṛthak dvayoḥ striyor guṇajyeṣṭhas teṣām āsīd yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: From Pāṇḍu were born five sons equal to gods, each from different mothers of two wives; the eldest among them in virtue was Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dharmād yudhiṣṭhiro jajñe mārutāt tu vṛkodaraḥ indrād dhanaṃjayaḥ śrīmān sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira was born from Dharma, Vṛkodara (Bhīma) from the wind god; from Indra was born the glorious Dhanañjaya (Arjuna), foremost among all bearers of weapons.

sanskrit: jajñāte rūpasaṃpannāv aśvibhyāṃ tu yamāv ubhau nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratau
english: The twin pair, endowed with beauty, were born from the Aśvins — Nakula and Sahadeva, devoted to the service of their elders.

sanskrit: tathā putraśataṃ jajñe dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dhīmataḥ duryodhanaprabhṛtayo yuyutsuḥ karaṇas tathā
english: Likewise a hundred sons were born to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra — headed by Duryodhana, and Yuyutsu, and Karana (Vikarṇa) likewise.

sanskrit: abhimanyuḥ subhadrāyām arjunād abhyajāyata svasrīyo vāsudevasya pautraḥ pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ
english: Abhimanyu was born from Arjuna through Subhadrā — the nephew of Vāsudeva, the grandson of the great-souled Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavebhyo 'pi pañcabhyaḥ kṛṣṇāyāṃ pañca jajñire kumārā rūpasaṃpannāḥ sarvaśastraviśāradāḥ
english: From the five Pāṇḍavas through Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) were born five princes, endowed with beauty and skilled in all weapons.

sanskrit: prativindhyo yudhiṣṭhirāt sutasomo vṛkodarāt arjunāc chrutakīrtis tu śatānīkas tu nākuliḥ
english: Prativindhya from Yudhiṣṭhira, Sutasoma from Vṛkodara (Bhīma), Śrutakīrti from Arjuna, and Śatānīka the son of Nakula.

sanskrit: tathaiva sahadevāc ca śrutasenaḥ pratāpavān hiḍimbāyāṃ ca bhīmena vane jajñe ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Likewise from Sahadeva came the valiant Śrutasena; and from Bhīma through Hiḍimba in the forest was born Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī drupadāj jajñe kanyā putratvam āgatā yāṃ yakṣaḥ puruṣaṃ cakre sthūṇaḥ priyacikīrṣayā
english: Śikhaṇḍin was born from Drupada — a girl who attained sonhood, whom the yaksha Sthuna made into a man out of desire to please.

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ vigrahe tasmin samāgacchan bahūny atha rājñāṃ śatasahasrāṇi yotsyamānāni saṃyuge
english: In that conflict of the Kurus, hundreds of thousands of kings assembled, about to fight in battle.

sanskrit: teṣām aparimeyāni nāmadheyāni sarvaśaḥ na śakyaṃ parisaṃkhyātuṃ varṣāṇām ayutair api ete tu kīrtitā mukhyā yair ākhyānam idaṃ tatam
english: Their names in their entirety cannot be reckoned — it is not possible to count them even in tens of thousands of years. But the chief ones have been named here, by whom this narrative is woven together.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca ya ete kīrtitā brahman ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ samyak tāñ śrotum icchāmi rājñaś cānyān suvarcasaḥ
english: Janamejaya said: O brahmin, those who have been named, and others who have not been fully named — I wish to hear about all of them properly, and about the other illustrious kings.

sanskrit: yadartham iha saṃbhūtā devakalpā mahārathāḥ bhuvi tan me mahābhāga samyag ākhyātum arhasi
english: For what purpose were these great warriors, equal to gods, born here upon the earth — that, O greatly blessed one, you ought to explain to me fully.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rahasyaṃ khalv idaṃ rājan devānām iti naḥ śrutam tat tu te kathayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā svayaṃbhuve
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: This is indeed a secret of the gods, O king — so we have heard. Yet I shall tell it to you, after bowing to the Self-born (Brahmā).

sanskrit: triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivīṃ kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṃ purā jāmadagnyas tapas tepe mahendre parvatottame
english: Having made the earth devoid of kshatriyas twenty-one times in the past, Jamadagni's son (Parashurama) practiced austerities on Mount Mahendra, the greatest of mountains.

sanskrit: tadā niḥkṣatriye loke bhārgaveṇa kṛte sati brāhmaṇān kṣatriyā rājan garbhārthinyo 'bhicakramuḥ
english: Then, when the world had been made devoid of kshatriyas by the descendant of Bhṛgu, O king, the kshatriya women approached brahmin men seeking to conceive.

sanskrit: tābhiḥ saha samāpetur brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ ṛtāv ṛtau naravyāghra na kāmān nānṛtau tathā
english: With them those brahmins of disciplined vows came together, O tiger among men, in the proper fertile season, not out of desire, nor out of season.

sanskrit: tebhyas tu lebhire garbhān kṣatriyās tāḥ sahasraśaḥ tataḥ suṣuvire rājan kṣatriyān vīryasaṃmatān kumārāṃś ca kumārīś ca punaḥ kṣatrābhivṛddhaye
english: From those brahmins those kshatriya women conceived by the thousands; then they gave birth, O king, to kshatriyas honored for their valor — both boys and girls — for the replenishment of the kshatriya order.

sanskrit: evaṃ tad brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatraṃ kṣatriyāsu tapasvibhiḥ jātam ṛdhyata dharmeṇa sudīrgheṇāyuṣānvitam catvāro 'pi tadā varṇā babhūvur brāhmaṇottarāḥ
english: Thus that kshatriya order, born from ascetic brahmins upon kshatriya women, prospered in righteousness, endowed with very long life; and all four social orders at that time were foremost in brahminic virtue.

sanskrit: abhyagacchann ṛtau nārīṃ na kāmān nānṛtau tathā tathaivānyāni bhūtāni tiryagyonigatāny api ṛtau dārāṃś ca gacchanti tadā sma bharatarṣabha
english: They approached women only in the proper season, not out of desire, nor out of season; likewise the other creatures, even those of animal birth, would approach their mates in season then, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato 'vardhanta dharmeṇa sahasraśatajīvinaḥ tāḥ prajāḥ pṛthivīpāla dharmavrataparāyaṇāḥ ādhibhir vyādhibhiś caiva vimuktāḥ sarvaśo narāḥ
english: Then those subjects grew in righteousness, living for hundreds of thousands of years, devoted to the vow of dharma, O protector of the earth; men were entirely free from mental anguish and physical disease.

sanskrit: athemāṃ sāgarāpāṅgāṃ gāṃ gajendragatākhilām adhyatiṣṭhat punaḥ kṣatraṃ saśailavanakānanām
english: Then the kshatriya order again ruled over this earth bounded by the ocean, traversed in its entirety with the gait of a great elephant, with its mountains, forests, and groves.

sanskrit: praśāsati punaḥ kṣatre dharmeṇemāṃ vasuṃdharām brāhmaṇādyās tadā varṇā lebhire mudam uttamām
english: When the kshatriya order again governed this wealth-bearing earth by dharma, the social orders headed by the brahmins attained supreme joy.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhodbhavān doṣān nirasya ca narādhipāḥ daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu dharmeṇa praṇayanto 'nvapālayan
english: The lords of men, having cast away the faults born of desire and anger, administered punishment to those deserving punishment in accordance with dharma, and thus protected their subjects.

sanskrit: tathā dharmapare kṣatre sahasrākṣaḥ śatakratuḥ svādu deśe ca kāle ca vavarṣāpyāyayan prajāḥ
english: While the kshatriya order was thus devoted to dharma, the thousand-eyed one of a hundred sacrifices (Indra) rained sweetly in the right place and season, nourishing the subjects.

sanskrit: na bāla eva mriyate tadā kaś cin narādhipa na ca striyaṃ prajānāti kaś cid aprāptayauvanaḥ
english: In that age, O lord of men, no child died in infancy; nor did any male know a woman before reaching youth.

sanskrit: evam āyuṣmatībhis tu prajābhir bharatarṣabha iyaṃ sāgaraparyantā samāpūryata medinī
english: Thus, O bull of the Bhāratas, this earth bounded by the ocean was abundantly filled with long-lived subjects.

sanskrit: ījire ca mahāyajñaiḥ kṣatriyā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ sāṅgopaniṣadān vedān viprāś cādhīyate tadā
english: The kshatriyas performed great sacrifices with abundant fees; and the brahmins studied the Vedas along with their supplementary texts and the Upaniṣads.

sanskrit: na ca vikrīṇate brahma brāhmaṇāḥ sma tadā nṛpa na ca śūdrasamābhyāśe vedān uccārayanty uta
english: The brahmins did not sell sacred knowledge in those days, O king; nor did they recite the Vedas in the proximity of those equal to shudras.

sanskrit: kārayantaḥ kṛṣiṃ gobhis tathā vaiśyāḥ kṣitāv iha na gām ayuñjanta dhuri kṛśāṅgāś cāpy ajīvayan
english: The vaishyas caused cultivation by means of oxen; they did not yoke a cow to the plough, nor did they keep thin-bodied animals alive for labor.

sanskrit: phenapāṃś ca tathā vatsān na duhanti sma mānavāḥ na kūṭamānair vaṇijaḥ paṇyaṃ vikrīṇate tadā
english: Men did not milk cows with suckling calves that were still drinking the froth-milk; nor did merchants sell goods with false weights in those days.

sanskrit: karmāṇi ca naravyāghra dharmopetāni mānavāḥ dharmam evānupaśyantaś cakrur dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Men, O tiger among men, performed deeds imbued with righteousness, keeping dharma always in view, devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: svakarmaniratāś cāsan sarve varṇā narādhipa evaṃ tadā naravyāghra dharmo na hrasate kva cit
english: All the social orders were absorbed in their own proper duties, O lord of men; thus in that age, O tiger among men, dharma did not diminish anywhere.

sanskrit: kāle gāvaḥ prasūyante nāryaś ca bharatarṣabha phalanty ṛtuṣu vṛkṣāś ca puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca
english: Cows gave birth in due season, and women likewise, O bull of the Bhāratas; trees bore flowers and fruits in their seasons.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtayuge samyag vartamāne tadā nṛpa āpūryata mahī kṛtsnā prāṇibhir bahubhir bhṛśam
english: Thus when the Kṛta age was proceeding properly in those days, O king, the entire earth was abundantly filled with many living beings.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudite loke mānuṣe bharatarṣabha asurā jajñire kṣetre rājñāṃ manujapuṃgava
english: Then, as the human world flourished, O bull of the Bhāratas, the asuras were born in the fields of kings, O foremost of men.

sanskrit: ādityair hi tadā daityā bahuśo nirjitā yudhi aiśvaryād bhraṃśitāś cāpi saṃbabhūvuḥ kṣitāv iha
english: For the daityas, having been repeatedly defeated in battle by the Ādityas and deprived of their sovereignty, came to be born here upon the earth.

sanskrit: iha devatvam icchanto mānuṣeṣu manasvinaḥ jajñire bhuvi bhūteṣu teṣu teṣv asurā vibho
english: Desiring divinity here and endowed with proud minds, O lord, the asuras were born among human beings on earth, in this and that creature.

sanskrit: goṣv aśveṣu ca rājendra kharoṣṭramahiṣeṣu ca kravyādeṣu ca bhūteṣu gajeṣu ca mṛgeṣu ca
english: Among cattle, among horses, O king of kings, among donkeys, camels, and buffaloes, among carnivorous creatures, among elephants and deer as well —

sanskrit: jātair iha mahīpāla jāyamānaiś ca tair mahī na śaśākātmanātmānam iyaṃ dhārayituṃ dharā
english: — by those who had been born here and those still being born, O guardian of the earth, this earth could no longer bear herself by her own strength.

sanskrit: atha jātā mahīpālāḥ ke cid balasamanvitāḥ diteḥ putrā danoś caiva tasmāl lokād iha cyutāḥ
english: Then certain kings were born endowed with great strength — sons of Diti and of Danu, fallen from that higher world to this one.

sanskrit: vīryavanto 'valiptās te nānārūpadharā mahīm imāṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ parīyur arimardanāḥ
english: Powerful and arrogant, bearing various forms, those crushers of foes roamed over this earth bounded by the ocean.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān vaiśyāñ śūdrāṃś caivāpy apīḍayan anyāni caiva bhūtāni pīḍayām āsur ojasā
english: They oppressed brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas, and shudras alike; they oppressed all other creatures as well with their power.

sanskrit: trāsayanto vinighnantas tāṃs tān bhūtagaṇāṃś ca te viceruḥ sarvato rājan mahīṃ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Terrifying and slaying these various groups of beings, they wandered over the earth in all directions, O king, by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: āśramasthān maharṣīṃś ca dharṣayantas tatas tataḥ abrahmaṇyā vīryamadā mattā madabalena ca
english: Assaulting great sages dwelling in their hermitages here and there, those enemies of brahmins, intoxicated with pride of valor and drunk with the intoxication of power —

sanskrit: evaṃ vīryabalotsiktair bhūr iyaṃ tair mahāsuraiḥ pīḍyamānā mahīpāla brahmāṇam upacakrame
english: — this earth, thus oppressed by those great asuras swollen with might and power, O protector of the earth, approached Brahmā.

sanskrit: na hīmāṃ pavano rājan na nāgā na nagā mahīm tadā dhārayituṃ śekur ākrāntāṃ dānavair balāt
english: For neither the wind, O king, nor the nagas, nor the mountains were able to bear this earth that had been forcibly overrun by the danavas.

sanskrit: tato mahī mahīpāla bhārārtā bhayapīḍitā jagāma śaraṇaṃ devaṃ sarvabhūtapitāmaham
english: Then the earth, O protector of the earth, weighed down by her burden and afflicted by fear, went for refuge to the god who is the grandfather of all beings.

sanskrit: sā saṃvṛtaṃ mahābhāgair devadvijamaharṣibhiḥ dadarśa devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāram avyayam
english: She saw the god Brahmā, the imperishable maker of the worlds, surrounded by the greatly blessed gods, twice-born ones, and great seers.

sanskrit: gandharvair apsarobhiś ca bandikarmasu niṣṭhitaiḥ vandyamānaṃ mudopetair vavande cainam etya sā
english: Being praised by gandharvas and apsarases engaged in the work of eulogizing, filled with joy — she approached and paid reverence to him.

sanskrit: atha vijñāpayām āsa bhūmis taṃ śaraṇārthinī saṃnidhau lokapālānāṃ sarveṣām eva bhārata
english: Then the earth, seeking refuge, presented her petition to him in the presence of all the world-guardians, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tat pradhānātmanas tasya bhūmeḥ kṛtyaṃ svayaṃbhuvaḥ pūrvam evābhavad rājan viditaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ
english: But the purpose of that earth's visit had already been known beforehand, O king, to the Self-born one of supreme nature, the one seated on the highest.

sanskrit: sraṣṭā hi jagataḥ kasmān na saṃbudhyeta bhārata surāsurāṇāṃ lokānām aśeṣeṇa manogatam
english: For how would the creator of the universe fail to know, O descendant of Bharata, the innermost thoughts of all worlds — of gods and asuras — without exception?

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahārāja bhūmiṃ bhūmipatir vibhuḥ prabhavaḥ sarvabhūtānām īśaḥ śaṃbhuḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: To her, O great king, spoke the lord of the earth, the all-pervading one, the source of all beings, the lord, the auspicious one, the Lord of Creatures (Brahmā).

sanskrit: yadartham asi saṃprāptā matsakāśaṃ vasuṃdhare tadarthaṃ saṃniyokṣyāmi sarvān eva divaukasaḥ
english: For the purpose for which you have come into my presence, O holder of wealth, for that purpose I shall set all the celestial ones to work.

sanskrit: ity uktvā sa mahīṃ devo brahmā rājan visṛjya ca ādideśa tadā sarvān vibudhān bhūtakṛt svayam
english: Having said this and dismissed the earth, O king, Brahmā the god, the creator of beings, himself gave instructions to all the wise ones.

sanskrit: asyā bhūmer nirasituṃ bhāraṃ bhāgaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak asyām eva prasūyadhvaṃ virodhāyeti cābravīt
english: He said: 'To remove the burden of this earth, be born separately, each in a portion, upon this very earth, for opposition against the asuras.'

sanskrit: tathaiva ca samānīya gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇān uvāca bhagavān sarvān idaṃ vacanam uttamam svair aṃśaiḥ saṃprasūyadhvaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ mānuṣeṣv iti
english: Likewise, having assembled the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases, the blessed one said this excellent word to them all: 'Be born as you please among human beings, each through your own portion.'

sanskrit: atha śakrādayaḥ sarve śrutvā suraguror vacaḥ tathyam arthyaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca tasya te jagṛhus tadā
english: Then Indra and all the others, having heard the word of their divine preceptor — true, purposeful, and beneficial — accepted it then.

sanskrit: atha te sarvaśo 'ṃśaiḥ svair gantuṃ bhūmiṃ kṛtakṣaṇāḥ nārāyaṇam amitraghnaḥ vaikuṇṭham upacakramuḥ
english: Then all of them, having resolved to go to the earth through their own portions, approached Nārāyaṇa the destroyer of foes at Vaikuṇṭha.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa cakragadāpāṇiḥ pītavāsāsitaprabhaḥ padmanābhaḥ surārighnaḥ pṛthucārvañcitekṣaṇaḥ
english: He who holds discus and mace in hand, clad in yellow, dark of radiance, lotus-naveled, destroyer of the foes of the gods, with broad and beautiful oblique eyes —

sanskrit: taṃ bhuvaḥ śodhanāyendra uvāca puruṣottamam aṃśenāvatarasveti tathety āha ca taṃ hariḥ
english: — to that Puruṣottama (Supreme Person), Indra, for the purification of the earth, said: 'Descend through a portion of yourself.' And Hari replied to him: 'So be it.'
